content: 1. Tseng CH, Chen TH, Wu JL, Lee TY, Borghi JA, Lin JT, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in 2023, published in JHEP Reports, to evaluate serious adverse events following the discontinuation of nucleos(t)ide analogues in individuals with chronic hepatitis B. 2. Hsu YC, Tseng CH, and Kao JH, in their 2023 publication in Clinical and Molecular Hepatology, emphasized the importance of safety considerations when withdrawing nucleos(t)ide analogues in patients with chronic hepatitis B, advocating for a first, do no harm approach. 3. Papatheodoridis GV, Lekakis V, Voulgaris T, Lampertico P, Berg T, Chan HLY, and colleagues systematically reviewed and performed a meta-analysis in 2022, published in Journal of Hepatology, to assess hepatitis B virus reactivation associated with new classes of immunosuppressants and immunomodulators, supplemented by expert opinions. 4. Karvellas CJ, Cardoso FS, Gottfried M, Reddy KR, Hanje AJ, Ganger D, and colleagues, in a 2017 study published in Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology, investigated the risk of death and acute liver failure associated with hepatitis B virus (HBV) following immunosuppression. 5. Tassopoulos NC, Papaevangelou GJ, Sjogren MH, Roumeliotou-Karayannis A, Gerin JL, and Purcell RH, in a 1987 study published in Gastroenterology, described the natural history of acute hepatitis B surface antigen-positive hepatitis in Greek adults. 6. Tillmann HL, Hadem J, Leifeld L, Zachou K, Canbay A, Eisenbach C, and colleagues reported on the safety and efficacy of lamivudine in patients with severe acute or fulminant hepatitis B in a multicenter study published in Journal of Viral Hepatitis in 2006. 7. Msomi N, Parboosing R, Wilkinson E, Giandhari J, Govender K, Chimukangara B, and colleagues, in a 2022 study published in Viruses, examined persistent hepatitis B viraemia with polymerase mutations in HIV/HBV co-infected patients on HBV-active antiretroviral therapy in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. 8. Yi W, Pan CQ, Li MH, Wan G, Lv YW, Liu M, and colleagues, in a 2018 study published in American Journal of Gastroenterology, identified characteristics and predictors of postpartum hepatitis flares in women with chronic hepatitis B. 9. Giles M, Visvanathan K, Lewin S, Bowden S, Locarnini S, Spelman T, and colleagues, in a 2015 study published in Gut, investigated clinical and virological predictors of hepatic flares in pregnant women with chronic hepatitis B. 10. Pan CQ, Han G, and Wang Y, in a 2016 publication in New England Journal of Medicine, discussed strategies for preventing peripartum hepatitis B transmission. 11. Ogunremi T, Defalco K, Johnston BL, Vearncombe M, Joffe AM, Cleghorn B, and colleagues summarized a new Canadian guideline in 2019, published in Canada Communicable Disease Report, aimed at preventing the transmission of bloodborne viruses from infected healthcare workers to patients. 12. Dolman GE, Koffas A, Phipps E, and Kennedy PTF, in a 2021 study published in Journal of Viral Hepatitis, reviewed the clinical and occupational health management of healthcare workers living with chronic hepatitis B, comparing UK policies with international practices. 13. Graham S, Guy RJ, Cowie B, Wand HC, Donovan B, Akre SP, and colleagues, in a 2013 systematic review and meta-analysis published in BMC Infectious Diseases, assessed the prevalence of chronic hepatitis B among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians following universal vaccination. 14. Batham A, Narula D, Toteja T, Sreenivas V, and Puliyel JM, in a 2007 systematic review and meta-analysis published in Indian Pediatrics, evaluated the prevalence of hepatitis B in India. 15. Scott JD and Garland N, in a 2008 study published in World Journal of Gastroenterology, explored chronic liver disease among Aboriginal North Americans. 16. McMahon BJ, in a 2004 publication in International Journal of Circumpolar Health, reviewed the epidemiology of viral hepatitis in Arctic populations. 17. Asselah T and Rizzetto M, in a 2023 article published in New England Journal of Medicine, provided an overview of hepatitis D virus infection, including its clinical implications and management strategies.
